items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: He used to stay up late at night and play duets with me. And more or less taught me most of the music that I knew, as far as formal training goes.

ctx.x: I want to get into that a little later on, more about your languages. But if we can get back to your early days, getting into trumpet playing and first bands, and that kind of thing.

Well, we had a good school band. We used to go to the contests, the county and state contests, and always win in our category. We had a very good teacher in grammar school. Then when I went to military school in high school we had a very good marching band there. We had a teacher there from the San Francisco Symphony who -- he played English horn himself but he was an old Italian gentleman and very inspiring man. He loved music and he got me to like it. He used to stay up late at night and play duets with me. And…

And while I was there I won the medal for music in military school. Then when I was -- see, in 1932 I started to work on the trumpet. While we were in school we had a little group and we played and somebody told me, you know, don't just play the melody, you have to play a little jazz and ad lib. And I said, well, what's that? And he said, did you ever hear Louis Armstrong, and I said, yes. He said, well, like he does. And I said, you know, that's what I'm trying to do.
